summary.tldr: Creates the Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime, expands some victims' rights, and sets out how those rights are to be put into practice.
what_it_does: Creates the Office of the Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime and makes the position a statutory office.
Sets the ombudsperson’s appointment, term, removal, pay, full-time service, and acting replacement rules.
Gives the office a mandate to help victims and families by giving information and referrals, reviewing complaints, and directing people to other services.
Limits complaint reviews about parole board decisions and certain Correctional Service of Canada decisions on transfers and release.
Requires annual reporting to the Minister, tabling in Parliament, and online publication, and allows the office to summon witnesses and require documents during reviews.
Amends the Canadian Victims Bill of Rights to enhance some victims’ rights and set up a framework for putting those rights into practice.
summary.background: The bill says the Federal Ombudsperson for Victims of Crime has existed since 2007 as a special adviser to the Minister of Justice. It also says the Canadian Victims Bill of Rights, adopted in 2015, gave the ombudsperson a mandate to review complaints about federal victim services and programs.
